missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend additional vitamin A; identify preformed retinol versus beta-carotene and quantify total exposure from prenatal and other products, with clinician/pharmacist review.
safety_exclusions: Do not recommend high-dose preformed vitamin A during pregnancy.
Do not assume retinol and beta-carotene have identical risk profiles.
Do not stop prescribed prenatal care without clinician advice.
professional_escalation_conditions: Pregnancy with preformed retinol use above recommended amounts, isotretinoin or other retinoid medicines, liver disease or suspected excessive exposure.
population_and_context: Pregnant people already taking vitamin A-containing supplements; preformed retinol exposure requires special attention because excessive intake can harm fetal development.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Distinguish preformed vitamin A from provitamin A carotenoids and follow local antenatal upper-limit guidance.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Vitamin A and pregnancy information describes teratogenic risk from excessive preformed vitamin A; exact product form and total exposure are essential. This justification remains draft pending source passage verification, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional review.
